import * as ns from 'data:text/javascript,export const a = 1; export default 2';
console.log(Object.keys(ns).length);

const mod = await import('data:text/javascript,export function url(){ return import.meta.url }');
console.log(mod.url() === import.meta.url ? 0 : 1);
While a module is suspended on top-level await, can a sibling that the parent imports separately still evaluate?
options: Yes. A sibling that is not waiting on that await can evaluate. The parent body starts once all of its static dependencies have finished
No. Top-level await freezes the whole graph until this module resumes
Yes, and the parent body runs interleaved with that wait
No. The sibling is not even instantiated

questions.text: What does the property descriptor of a namespace export say, and can an importer write to it?
options: writable: false, configurable: true. Assignment succeeds silently
writable: true, configurable: false. Assignment and delete still throw TypeError. Only the module that declared the binding can change it
writable: true, configurable: true. The importer can store a new value
There is no descriptor: an export is not an own property

questions.text: When can a function on the other side of a cycle read a let or const?
options: Only before initialization. After that the binding is closed
Never. The cycle keeps the binding unavailable for the rest of the program
After that binding's initializer has run. The read is live and sees later assignments. A direct read during initialization throws ReferenceError
Immediately at instantiation, before any body, and the final value is already there

questions.text: What does import() resolve a string that starts with ./ against?
options: process.cwd(), because the string is computed at runtime
The page URL, even when the call is inside a nested module
The URL of the current module, like a static import. Only the string itself is computed at runtime

questions.text: At the top level of a module, this refers to globalThis.
await inside an export function suspends the module graph the way top-level await does.
A syntax error in the target module makes import() throw on the line that calls it.
export * as name from also adds a default export to the current module.
How does instantiating a module differ from evaluating its body?
questions.answer: Instantiation creates the bindings: function is already initialized, var is undefined, let and const are not. Evaluation then runs the bodies. A cyclic read of let before its initializer throws during evaluation.

How do you load a module only when one branch of a condition runs?
questions.answer: Call import() inside that branch. A static import is unconditional and can only appear at the top level.

questions.text: What key does the module map use for a module?
questions.answer: The absolute URL after the specifier is resolved. The same source text at another URL is a different instance.
